                    ### Question
                    A 27-year-old woman goes to the genetic counseling clinic after having a child with Down syndrome. In the child, a trisomy 21 with translocation 21/21 inherited from the mother is identified. What would be the risk of recurrence of Down syndrome in the future children of this woman?

                    ### Options
                    opa. The risk of recurrence will be 10-15%, as in the rest of translocations.
opb. 100% of viable fetuses will be born with Down syndrome.
opc. The risk of recurrence will be very low (12%).
opd. The risk of recurrence will be 50%.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In cases where a parent carries a 21/21 translocation, all gametes produced will contain an extra chromosome 21. This is because the translocation results in gametes that either have two chromosome 21s or none, but viable gametes will always have two chromosome 21s. Therefore, all viable offspring will inherit an extra chromosome 21, leading to Down syndrome. This aligns with the consensus that 100% of viable fetuses will be born with Down syndrome if the mother has a 21/21 translocation. The retrieved evidence path, while broad, supports the understanding that germ cells with altered chromosomal arrangements can lead to conditions like trisomy. Thus, option 'opb' is correct: 100% of viable fetuses will be born with Down syndrome.
